newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma's Suu Kyi claims 800 supporters detained.
newsitem.headline: Burma's Suu Kyi claims 800 supporters detained.

text.p: Democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi said on Wednesday that up to 800 of her National League for Democracy (NLD) members and supporters had been arrested by the Burmese military government since last Thursday.

Suu Kyi told reporters at a house a few blocks from her residence that the latest government crackdown and its decision to bar access to her residence was expected and would help boost her legitimacy.

"What has happened over the last week has been a great help to us," a relaxed-looking Suu Kyi said. "People are fed up with this kind of stupid behaviour and the international community agrees now the SLORC is getting worse not better."

The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) said it detained 559 NLD members or supporters in a crackdown to stop a September 27-29 party congress. It also barricaded the road leading to her house to prevent access to her.
"We think it is nearer 800," she said when told of the government's number of detentions. She vowed to hold another party congress without seeking permission from the SLORC.
